I FIRST SUSPECTED A DEFECT - the number looks unconditional while print restricts it to sight - and traced the application path rather than guessing: src/rules/derive.ts:343 takes `Math.max(abpPerception, mpSenseSkillItemBonus, passiveItemBonus(c, db, 'perception'))`, and passiveItemBonus (:262-283) reads `pe[kind]` off every in-use item's passiveEffects, so yes, the +1 lands on the Perception total unconditionally. THEN I MEASURED WHETHER THAT IS THE CONVENTION OR THE DEFECT, which settled it: 20 items in core.json carry BOTH a `passiveEffects.perception` number AND a sight-restricted Perception star - wardrobe-stone-greater, eye-of-the-unseen, all three eye slashes, four clarity-goggles, four mirror-goggles, two spectacles, three obsidian-goggles, white-cleomes-eye, shining-hackle. Several of those stars state the design intent in so many words: clarity-goggles-greater and every mirror-goggles read "visual Perception checks only (already in your total; not hearing or scent)". So number-plus-caveat-star IS the authored pattern for a per-check restriction, it is the same split WG uses (value + text), and eye-slash-greater follows it exactly, at the right magnitude, with its two siblings scaled 2 and 3. NOTHING TO FIX. Note the contrast that makes this a real distinction rather than a rationalisation: the Unifying Emblem's Diplomacy +1 is starred with NO number, correctly - its condition is a build-state fork ("if you already know Shoanti") that our engine cannot gate a passiveEffects value on, whereas Eye Slash's is a per-check restriction, which is exactly what a star beside an applied number is for. Non-blocking cosmetic difference, deliberately not specced: their sense note says "you can see blood in color" (the darkvision clause) while ours says "see four times farther than normal" (the distance clause) - both are display-only sense strings and the full prose is in core-descriptions.json either way.

Their side is one conditional over two branches: IF the character has Quick Repair, a filtered select over 1st-level Skill feats; ELSE giveAbilityBlock(Quick Repair). Ours shipped only the ELSE — FEAT_FEAT_GRANTS['engine-bay'] grants the feat, and the granted-feat walk dedupes against feats already held, so a character who arrived with Quick Repair had the grant silently DROPPED and received nothing in its place. That silence is the entire content of the printed 'instead'. Built `FeatPickSpec.onlyIfHasFeat`, honoured at the pick-grant site in build.ts: the two branches are mutually exclusive by construction, since the gate is true exactly when the static grant is dropped as a duplicate. 5 tests.
